result:
**Solution 1 (binom(n-1,2)+2): REJECT.** The proposed extremal graph, K_{n-1} plus a vertex v joined to two clique vertices u and w, does contain a HIST. Make v a leaf attached to u, and take a star centered at u in the K_{n-1}. Then u has degree n-1 ≥ 3, and every other vertex has degree 1. The solution admits this itself and then asserts the bound anyway, without a valid construction. The claimed maximum is not supported.

**Solution 2 (2n-4): REJECT.** K_{2,n-2} is 2-connected and HIST-free, since the n-2 vertices on the large side have degree 2 and so must be leaves, which leaves the two hubs disconnected unless a degree-2 vertex links them. But it is far from extremal. For n ≥ 13, the construction in Solution 3 already has binom(n-3,2)+4 > 2n-4 edges, so 2n-4 cannot be the maximum.

**Solution 3 (binom(n-3,2)+4): ACCEPT.** I checked the construction directly. Take a clique K_{n-3} and a path v₁–a–b–c–v₂. The vertices a, b, c have degree 2, so in any HIST they must be leaves. But b's only neighbours are a and c, so b's tree edge goes to a or c, and that vertex then has tree-degree 1 and cannot connect to the rest of the tree. So no HIST exists. The graph is 2-connected with binom(n-3,2)+4 edges. The optimality argument is only sketched, but I checked the natural competitor (a degree-3 vertex x joined to two clique vertices plus a leaf z), and it does contain a HIST. The value binom(n-3,2)+4 also matches the threshold binom(n-3,2)+5 that I recall from the HIST literature, though I could not verify that citation here.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: REJECT
VERDICT 3: ACCEPT
